newsitem.title: USA: Columbia Gas files Ohio choice proposal.
newsitem.headline: Columbia Gas files Ohio choice proposal.

text.p: Columbia Gas of Ohio said Friday it has filed its "Customer Choice" program, with the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio, proposing to that residential and small commercial customers have the option of purchasing natural gas from suppliers other than Columbia.
The Columbia Gas System Inc subsidiary said the proposed program is voluntary, and unless customers choose another company, it will remain their natural gas supplier.
If approved by the commission, Columbia said, the program will be introduced in the greater Toledo area where about 170,000 customers will be eligible.

It will be offered in the remainder of the company's Ohio service territory following an evaluation and customer surveys in Toledo. Toledo was chosen for the introduction of the program since it is representative of Columbia's customer base around the state.
Columbia said it will kick off a public education campaign in November, with individual suppliers announcing their programs in mid-January 1997.
Toledo-area customers will be able to take delivery of gas through the suppliers in early April 1997, the utility said.
It said the "Customer Choice" program was developed in cooperation with the commission, the Office of the Consumers' Counsel, various Ohio cities and school districts, and Columbia customer groups.

"Columbia was the first gas utility in Ohio to make this type of program available to its industrial customers in the early 1970s and it's been a great success. We're pleased to be an industry leader in offering the same options and benefits to residential and small commercial customers," the company said. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
